messages:
maria_support: FYI - Acme reported p99 spikes during their monthly invoice run (~10:30-10:45 UTC). They see p95 up from ~60ms to ~1.2s and p99 up to 6-8s. Posting quick summary and repro.

maria_support: Timeline: invoice job kicks off at 10:36, request fanout ~1200 concurrent requests routed to dedicated pool 'acme-prod'. Observed attach latencies and some attach timeouts. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/acme/dedicated-latency (redacted)

maria_support: Error snippets from their logs:
```
attach_error: attach_timeout
gpu_boot: cold_start 89s
auth: 401 transient
```

maria_support: Repro steps they ran:
1) kickoff 800-1200 concurrent requests
2) model: owl-13b-quant
3) seq len ~512

sam_sre: Looking. Any deploys or scale policy changes around 10:00?

maria_support: No deploys. We did flip minpool=0 for acme-prod last night to save cost (⚠️). Possibly related.

jordan_platform: Oof — minpool=0 + large scheduled fanout = cold GPU starts and an attach storm. That can back up the attach queue and saturate auth proxy. Recommend temporary mitigation: set minpool=2 for acme-prod and bump reserved concurrency to 50 for the invoice route.

lee_oncall: I'm executing the dedicated-warmup playbook now (runbook id: warmup-2026-04). Prewarming acme-prod and enabling priority queue for invoice route.

deploybot: prewarm job started for pool=acme-prod; job_id=prewarm-8842

sam_sre: Infra metrics: attach handler backlog spiked at ~10:38, attach success rate down to 67%. Auth proxy error rate increased concurrent with attach flood — looks like token refreshs are saturating. Are they hitting token rate limits or auth rotation?

maria_support: Customer says tokens unchanged; we rotated keys last week. I have trace ids if you need them.

jordan_platform: Short-term fixes we applied or recommend immediately:
- increase minpool to 2-4 for acme-prod
- enable preemptive warmup for invoice route (scheduled prewarm before job)
- add model fallback: allow owl-13b-legacy-8bit for invoice route to avoid long tail latencies

sam_sre: Longer-term actions: enforce minpool floor for heavy scheduled routes, add per-customer attach quotas, and add randomized backoff to autoscaler to avoid synchronized scaleups.

anya_custsuccess: Notified Acme, told them we are prewarming and may throttle their job if spikes persist. They asked for ETA on fix.

lee_oncall: ETA ~10-20m for warmup; if p99 remains >2s we'll reroute to fallback model and keep them updated.

maria_support: After prewarm: p95 down to ~140ms, p99 down to ~700ms. Attach timeouts dropped to 0. Customer confirmed invoices completed successfully.

sam_sre: Marking mitigated. Action items: platform to add per-customer attach quotas + enforce scheduled-route minpool; support to advise customers about minpool for heavy fanout jobs.

jordan_platform: Filing RFC for 'scheduled-route-minpool' in eng-platform; will include simulation and cost tradeoffs.

maria_support: Thanks all :heart: Closing once RFC is created.

lee_oncall: Adding postmortem note: incident_acme_invoice_1719876543

maria_support: +1
